sn6.14:2.3: Sikhī means “halo” or “crown”. [dn14:1.12.4]() says Aruṇa was his father, and Pabhāvatī his mother. The son of King Dawn and Queen Radiant in the City of the Dawn, Sikhī is the streaming rays of sunrise. These names recall a solar myth.
sn6.14:2.4: Abhibhū (“Victor”) and Sambhava (“son of Śambhu the blessed”) are also at [dn14:1.9.2](). _Śambhu_ is commonly found in the Rig Veda in the sense, “blessing, benefit”, and became a common name or epithet of gods, etc.
